title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is the end of a general lemma and the start of its application. The lemma is a 'rigidification by trivial cohomology' statement inside the Longue Marche continuation, on the Galois action on the abelianised tripod.

General set-up (previous and this page):
- Γ is a (profinite) group and M a Γ-module.
- Γ̃ = Im(Γ → Aut(M)).
- M̃ is a given extension of Γ by M (a pro-extension, in practice the abelianised arithmetic fundamental group).
- The objects 𝔛' are pairs (E, Θ_M̃): E is an M-torsor and Θ_M̃ is an action of M̃ on E compatible with the M-action. The model case is E = the set of splittings, with M̃ acting by conjugation.

Corollary on the previous page. Assume (292): H^0(Γ̃, M) = M^Γ = 0 and H^1(Γ̃, M) = 0. Then any two splittings of a split extension of Γ̃ by M are conjugate by a unique element of M. So the category of pairs (E, Θ) is rigid: an object is determined up to unique isomorphism. Its isomorphism classes ('données d'isomorphie') correspond bijectively to quotient groups M̃̃ of M̃ such that:
- (a) M → M̃ → M̃̃ is injective, giving an extension (293) 1 → M → M̃̃ → Γ' := M̃̃/M → 1;
- (b) Γ' acts faithfully on M, i.e. Γ' ≅ Γ̃;
- (c) the extension M̃̃ of Γ̃ by M is split (class 0 in H^2(Γ̃, M)).

Conversely, given such a quotient, take E = the set of splittings of M̃̃ → Γ̃, with M̃ acting through M̃̃ by conjugation. By (292) the restriction to M ⊂ M̃ makes E an M-torsor (the manuscript writes 'E-torseur', a slip for M-torseur).

Application (bottom of page and next page). Γ = Gal(Q̄/Q) (× S_3), and M = M^∧ is the abelianised profinite π_1 of P^1 − {0,1,∞}, essentially Ẑ(1)^2 as the reduced permutation representation of S_3. Then Γ̃ ≅ Ẑ* × S_3, with Ẑ* coming from the cyclotomic character. In n°120 he had checked (292) and constructed certain split extensions G̃_{ρ,σ} of Γ̃ by M^∧.

The next page concludes:
- the quotient M_{0,3} → G̃ built in n°11 satisfies (a)–(c);
- hence it yields a canonical (up to unique iso) pro-cover of the stack (M_{0,3}, S_3) ≅ M'_{1,1} over Q, whose base change to Q̄ is the universal abelian cover of the tripod;
- this is then to be compared with the Fermat tower, which provides such an object explicitly.

In short: a canonical, S_3-equivariant Q-model of the maximal abelian cover of P^1 − {0,1,∞}, pinned down by cohomological rigidity.
errors: 'fait de E un E-torseur' is a slip for 'M-torseur'.

The vanishing H^1(Ẑ* × S_3, Ẑ(1)^2 reduced rep) = 0 is not reproved here (it is referred back to n°120). Away from 2 it follows from Sah's lemma with the central element −1 ∈ Ẑ*. The 2-primary part needs a separate argument, using S_3 and the units of Z_2, which is not visible on this page.

ideas.what: Rigidity: if H^0 = H^1 = 0, splittings of a split extension form an M-torsor with unique conjugating elements. Hence torsors with compatible M̃-action are classified by quotients M̃̃ of M̃ with M injective, Γ' ≅ Γ̃ acting faithfully, and the extension split.
ideas.modern_name: Non-abelian cohomology of group extensions / classification of splittings by H^1; rigidification of torsors
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard (Eilenberg–MacLane, Hochschild–Serre; Giraud for non-abelian cohomology)
ideas.where_published: Similar formalism in SGA1 Exp. XIII and in Giraud; this exact lemma is unknown to me in print

ideas.what: Canonical Q-structure (equivariant for S_3, i.e. on the stack (M_{0,3}, S_3) ≅ M'_{1,1}) on the maximal abelian pro-cover of P^1 − {0,1,∞}, characterised by rigidity, to be compared with the Fermat tower.
ideas.modern_name: Galois action on the abelianised/metabelian fundamental group of the tripod; Fermat curves and Jacobi sums
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara (1986, Annals: profinite braid groups, Galois representations and complex multiplications); Anderson (hyperadelic gamma function, 1989); Coleman
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme mentions the M_{0,3} / M_{1,1} and Galois action programme only in general terms

missed.claim: Grothendieck characterises the Fermat tower, viewed as a Q-form of the abelian universal cover of the tripod descended to the S_3-quotient stack M'_{1,1}, by a cohomological rigidity principle: H^0 = H^1(Ẑ* × S_3, M^∧) = 0 forces uniqueness. This is a structural explanation of the canonicity of the Fermat-tower model, parallel to but independent of Ihara's power-series approach.
missed.quote: Pour un tel quotient M̃̃ de M̃, on s'imagine E comme l'ensemble de tous les scindages de l'extension M̃̃ de Γ̃ par M
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It offers a uniqueness/rigidity framing for Galois-equivariant models of abelian covers of moduli stacks, which is relevant to anabelian reconstructions of the metabelian quotient of GT. It is likely only a modest addition to Ihara–Anderson.

deep.surprise_reason: The general lemma is routine group cohomology. The application (a canonical S_3-equivariant Q-model of the abelianised tripod cover compared with the Fermat tower) is an independent, early Grothendieck treatment of territory largely covered by Ihara and Anderson in the 1980s. It is a nice detail but not a new result.
transcription_corrections: '(forgeant [?] M→M̃→M̃̃)' is unclear in the image; the reading is probably '(composé ...)' or '(factorisant ...)', and the intended meaning is the composite M → M̃ → M̃̃.
In c) the extension is M̃̃ (double tilde), not M̃.
'de E un E-torseur' is what is written, but it should read M-torseur.
'certaines 𝔊_{ρ,σ}' is likely 'certaines extensions G̃_{ρ,σ}' (with tilde), consistent with the next page's G̃_{q,σ}.
